crime: One prisoner spent her hours in the lounge knitting winter scarves for the others. {WITCH_NAME} drew a chalk door on the wall of the knitter's cell, and it swung open onto a sunlit kitchen that the two of them shared.
One day the knitter gave her a sweater one size too big. "So it still fits you next winter."
In an autumn of {WITCH_NAME}'s childhood, her mother had knitted her sweaters in sizes she had not yet grown into, and was gone before the first frost.

After lockup, {WITCH_NAME} drew a door on her own cell wall, crossed the kitchen, and came out into the knitter's cell. She strangled the knitter with one of her own scarves and hanged her by it from the barred cell door. Then she went back through the kitchen and wiped the chalk door off her own wall.

At the morning unlock, the prisoners found the knitter hanging from her barred cell door. She had been locked in alone all night, and the chalk door on her wall opened onto a kitchen with no other door. They ruled that she had hanged herself.
Then one prisoner found a tea ring on the kitchen tablecloth. Her own cup had left it there, at the tea {WITCH_NAME} once hosted behind a door in the lounge.
In the trial court, the prisoners saw it: every door {WITCH_NAME} drew opened onto the same sunlit kitchen, and that kitchen had put her inside the locked cell.
fields.epitaph: One size too big was never a goodbye; it was a promise to be there when it fit.
execution: The execution stand chains her upright, facing an iron wall. A chalk door is drawn on it, with sunlight spilling out from underneath.
The wall rolls forward. It reaches her chest and keeps rolling, and the door never opens.
Pressed flat against the closed door, she stops moving.

magic.name: The Daydream Door
magic.text: She draws a chalk door on any wall, and it opens onto a sunlit room she imagines.
